newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian interbank rates steady, liquidity better.
newsitem.headline: Croatian interbank rates steady, liquidity better.

text.p: Croatian interbank rates were steady to lower on Monday thanks to improved money market liquidity that left some surpluses again after days of strains, dealers said.
But banks increased their Lombard borrowing from the central bank to 124.6 million kuna from around 30 last Friday.
Fresh money market loans totalled 22 million kuna by 0900 GMT and were mostly call money borrowings at between a lower 9.0, 9.5 and 10 percent.
One one-week loan was granted at an unchanged 11 percent.
There were no 60-day funds on offer, leaving one bank short despite a 50 million kuna surplus in supply.
To square their shortfalls at the end of Friday, two banks borowed 71 million kuna in inter-bank deals. This brought overall balances of the banking sector to a higher 584 million kuna.
Two banks bought 39.9 million kuna in weekend overnight trade on the money market to maintain their mandatory reserves. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb Newsroom 385-1-4557075
